mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 1.0% compresses equity valuations through higher discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the market prices in sustained monetary tightening.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 1.0% and 20-day returns are positive in >55% of cases, or mean return difference from baseline is not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate exceeding 1.5% signals aggressive monetary tightening, increasing equity risk premiums and driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 1.5% and 20-day returns are positive in >55% of instances, or mean return difference from baseline is not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings growth accelerates.
failure_condition: Joint growth in HOUST and RSAFS does not produce positive 60-day returns in >60% of cases, or interaction term regression coefficient is not negative with p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate rising above 4.0% signals labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate profits, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days during monetary tightening cycles.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 4.0% during monetary tightening cycles does not yield negative 20-day returns in >60% of cases, or mean return difference from baseline is not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO) indicates weakening manufacturing activity, reducing corporate earnings growth expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO decline (qoq) does not produce negative 5-day returns in >60% of cases, or mean return difference from baseline is not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 4.5% signals imminent economic slowdown, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as recession risk increases.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 4.5% and 20-day returns are positive in >55% of instances, or mean return difference from baseline is not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 240) combined with elevated interest rates (FEDFUNDS > 1.0%) indicates persistent inflation, prompting restrictive policy that depresses equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Joint condition CPIAUCSL > 240 and FEDFUNDS > 1.0% does not produce negative 60-day returns in >60% of cases, or interaction term regression coefficient is not negative with p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO) during recessionary regimes (GDPC1 contraction) signals deepening economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as earnings weakness intensifies.
failure_condition: INDPRO decline during recessionary regimes (GDPC1 contraction) does not yield negative 60-day returns in >60% of cases, or mean return difference from baseline is not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.05).
